findings.item: ROOT OF THE CHAIN: Goldfeld2 (Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026) is the sole upstream manuscript of the whole BSD chain. Its Theorem 1.1 [The 2-converse] (verbatim: 'For every elliptic curve E/Q with c_2(E) in {0,1}, a(E)=r(E)=c_2(E), Sha(E/Q) is finite') and Theorem 1.2 [Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture] are imported as 'established' by SelmerConverse (02-reduction.tex ll.36-58: 'We use the following two established results ... These are \citet[Theorems~1.1 and~1.2]{OpenAIGoldfeldDensity2026}'), by ExactBSD (02-classical.tex l.110: 'We use the theorem at the scope stated in \cite[Theorem~1.2]{Goldfeld}'), by TwoPrimary (corollaries only) and by MeanRank. Theorem 1.2 of Goldfeld2 is itself deduced (00-introduction.tex ll.49-53 and 11-conclusions.tex l.68) from the published-literature preprint A. Smith, 'The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture implies Goldfeld's conjecture', arXiv:2503.17619 version 1, Theorem 1.1 (unrefereed arXiv preprint, human author). No Lean formalization exists for Goldfeld2 or any paper in the chain (lean/formalization.yaml: no hit; no lean/docs/002.md, 004.md, 006.md).
findings.why_relevant: Every rank/finiteness/BSD claim in the family 002/006 chain is only as good as Goldfeld2 Thm 1.1 (the pointwise 2-converse, 'the main work of this paper') plus Smith 2025 v1. Any use of the chain for the seed (e.g. #Sha(E^{-7}/Q)) must grade Goldfeld2 first. Grade: IMPORTED_PREPRINT at best (K-GRADE).

findings.item: ExactBSD Theorem 1.1 (build/sections/01-introduction.tex ll.46-60, verbatim hypothesis 'Let E/Q be an elliptic curve and let q be any prime. If s_q(E) in {0,1}, then r(E)=a(E)=s_q(E), #Sha(E/Q)<infty, and ... L^{(r)}(E,1)/r! = Omega_E Reg_E #Sha prod c_ell / #E(Q)_tors^2') imports, in its proof body and not only in the intro: (i) C = SelmerConverse Thm 1.1 restated as Theorem [Unrestricted low-corank converse] classical:low-corank ('This is \cite[Theorem~1.1]{C}', 02-classical.tex l.36); (ii) B = TwoPrimary Thm 1.1 restated as Theorem [Two-primary leading term] classical:two-primary ('This is \cite[Theorem~1.1]{B}', l.50); (iii) Goldfeld Thm 1.2 restated as Theorem [Analytic twist densities] classical:twist-density (l.110). Beyond statements it uses INTERNAL lemmas of B and C inside proofs: B Lemmas 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.10, 12.1, Cor 12.2, Section 4 (K5), Section 8 'CM disk coordinates', Section 9 'Inert derivative identity' eq (K) (03-models.tex ll.312,445,589; 04-vertical.tex l.300; 05-single.tex ll.30,79,198,315; 06-pair.tex ll.218,843,885); C Lemmas 4.2, 4.4, 4.5, 6.1, 6.2, 6.4, 7.1-7.3, 8.6, 8.8, 9.5, Prop 8.5, Prop 9.7, eqs (4.1)-(4.2),(4.10),(5.6),(5.8),(5.10),(6.7),(8.10),(8.11) (07-theta.tex ll.24-966; 08-extraction.tex ll.63-975). ExactBSD's own new content per l.65-67: 'The new assertion proved here is the exact valuation of the leading-term formula at every odd prime'.
findings.why_relevant: Verifying ExactBSD requires verifying the internals (not just the headline theorems) of TwoPrimary and SelmerConverse. ExactBSD is the only paper in the chain whose conclusion is the full leading-term formula at odd primes, i.e. the only one that could bear on #Sha(E^{-7}/Q) at p>=3. It is cited by no other manuscript (sink of the graph).

findings.item: SelmerConverse Theorem 1.1 [The unrestricted low-corank Selmer converse] (01-introduction.tex ll.24-36: 'For every elliptic curve A_0/Q, every prime p, and r in {0,1}, s_p(A_0)=r implies a(A_0)=rank A_0(Q)=r, #Sha(A_0/Q)<infty') depends logically on Goldfeld2: 'The present proof uses two distinct results of \citet{OpenAIGoldfeldDensity2026}: the unrestricted converse at 2 settles that prime, while the analytic twist-density theorem supplies the auxiliary fields for the odd-prime argument' (01-introduction.tex ll.126-130); reduction step 'By Theorem~\ref{thm:two-converse-input}, we may assume p>2' (02-reduction.tex l.60). Other imports named there: Dokchitser-Dokchitser 2010 Thm 1.4 (p-parity), BCDT 2001, Gross-Zagier 1986, Kolyvagin 1990. No other OAI manuscript is cited by SelmerConverse.
findings.why_relevant: The p=2 case is NOT proved in SelmerConverse; it is wholly Goldfeld2's. The odd-p case uses Goldfeld2 Thm 1.2 for auxiliary fields. For the seed, SelmerConverse cannot apply to E (s_p(E)>=2 for all p, K-RANK2); for E^{-7} its conclusions (rank 0, Sha finite) are already PROVED in the lab by Gross-Zagier-Kolyvagin, so it adds nothing there.

findings.item: TwoPrimary Theorem 1.1 [thm:main] (01-introduction.tex ll.~40-70: for E/Q with s_2(E)<=1: ranks equal s_2, #Sha<infty, Q_E in Q_{>0}, v_2(Q_E)=v_2(#Sha(E/Q)); 'There is no restriction on E[2] or on the reduction of E at two') cites NO OAI manuscript in its proof body (parser: only 3 OAI cite uses in the whole paper, all in corollaries). Corollary [An any-prime input criterion] cor:any-prime-bsd (ll.72-95) imports SelmerConverse Thm 1.1 ('By \cite[Theorem~1.1]{OpenAIAllPrimeSelmer2026}, rank E(Q)=r:=s_p(E) and the whole group Sha(E/Q) is finite', l.85). Corollary cor:quadratic-twist-density (15-conclusion.tex ll.~80-131) imports Goldfeld2 'proof of Theorem 1.2' for Selmer-corank densities (l.121).
findings.why_relevant: TwoPrimary's headline 2-adic BSD formula is citation-independent of the other OAI papers (its 2-converse content is argued internally; it still must be verified on its own, ~15 sections). Only its corollaries depend on SelmerConverse/Goldfeld2. For the seed: E^{-7} has s_2=0, so Thm 1.1 (if correct) gives v_2(#Sha(E^{-7}/Q)) = v_2(Q_{E^{-7}}), an explicitly computable quantity; E itself is excluded (s_2(E)=2).

findings.item: MeanRank Theorem 1.1 [thm:mean] (introduction.tex ll.23-29) = (Goldfeld2 Thm 1.2 as eq:density-input, introduction.tex ll.34-44: 'For the analytic mean theorem, (density-input) is the only input from the companion manuscript') + its own tail estimate Thm 1.2 [thm:tail] 'whose proof is independent of (density-input)'. Corollary cor:algebraic-moments (algebraic.tex ll.10-30) imports Goldfeld2 Thm 1.2's rank-equality clause AND the published-literature preprint Koymans-Smith, 'Tamagawa Ratios and Unbounded Selmer Moments', arXiv:2606.31649v1, Theorem 1.4 (references.bib ll.27-35). arXiv number 2606.31649 (June 2026) could not be verified offline.
findings.why_relevant: MeanRank is downstream of Goldfeld2 only; nothing in it concerns a single curve's Sha, so it is irrelevant to FIN/ORDER9/Q36 except as part of the density picture. Flag: dependence on an unverified 2026 arXiv preprint in the algebraic corollary.

findings.item: Pointwise2 (rational two-torsion 2-converse) cites Goldfeld2 Thm 1.1 only expositorily: 'The broader companion \cite[Theorem~1.1]{OpenAIGoldfeldTwoConverse2026} proves the 2-converse without the rational-two-torsion hypothesis. Here we give a separate full treatment ... the broader converse is not an input to the proof.' (introduction.tex ll.39-43). It cites no other OAI manuscript. CONTENTS.md lists Pointwise2 under family 004 (Hilbert's tenth problem over Q, CONTENTS.md l.116), not family 002; the Hilbert-10 manuscripts (Sept-24 and Oct-6) import both Pointwise2 and Goldfeld2.
findings.why_relevant: Pointwise2 is citation-independent of the chain and is the only paper in the set whose hypotheses (nonzero rational 2-torsion: seed E(Q)_tors = Z/2 holds) partially match the seed, but its Selmer hypothesis s_2<=1 fails for E (s_2(E)=2) and is already-known content for E^{-7}. Not usable for the seed obligations (K-RANK2).

findings.item: NO CYCLE. Dependency DAG among the six (edge = A imports a result of B in a proof or as a stated input): ExactBSD -> {SelmerConverse (C), TwoPrimary (B), Goldfeld2}; SelmerConverse -> {Goldfeld2}; TwoPrimary -> {SelmerConverse, Goldfeld2} (corollaries only; main theorem has no OAI edge); MeanRank -> {Goldfeld2}; Pointwise2 -> {} (Goldfeld2 expository only); Goldfeld2 -> {} (imports Smith 2025 arXiv:2503.17619v1 Thm 1.1 from the literature). The reciprocal citations Goldfeld2 -> TwoPrimary (Thm 1.1, Cor 16.1), Goldfeld2 -> SelmerConverse (Thm 1.1) and Goldfeld2 -> MeanRank (Thms 1.1-1.2) occur ONLY in Goldfeld2's intro subsection 'Consequences and companion results' (00-introduction.tex ll.76-101), phrased as 'The separate companion ... proves', 'A subsequent companion ... Its proof uses the 2-converse and analytic twist densities established here', 'This consequence is \citet[Corollary~16.1]{OpenAITwoPrimaryBSD2026}'; Goldfeld2's Theorems 1.1/1.2 do not claim the mean rank or the BSD formula, and its 11-conclusions.tex cites no OAI key. Topological order: Goldfeld2 < SelmerConverse < TwoPrimary < ExactBSD; MeanRank and Pointwise2 are leaves off Goldfeld2. All OAI keys in the six resolve only to manuscripts among the six; all targets exist and none carries a withdrawal notice.
findings.why_relevant: Rules out circular justification among the six; the chain is linear with a single root (Goldfeld2 + Smith 2025). Verification effort for ExactBSD therefore = Goldfeld2 + SelmerConverse + TwoPrimary + ExactBSD, with no shortcut.

findings.item: VERSION DIFFS (diff -r on build/ dirs, read-only): all six Sept/Oct-3 -> Oct-6/7 updates change ONLY (a) the \date line in main.tex/paper.tex and (b) the OAI href/label pointers in references.tex/.bib (September-23/24 -> October-6/7 directory names), plus (c) in ExactBSD the single intro line 01-introduction.tex:134 '\cite{B,C,Dv}' -> '\cite{B,C}'. No theorem statement, hypothesis, proof text, section file or bibliography entry (other than those pointers) changed in any of the six. The README 'Version note' wording ('updates citations to revised manuscripts in this collection') is therefore not evidence of any proof repair in this family; history.md confirms the six are among the '13 additional manuscripts updated to cite the revised editions' except ExactBSD, which is among the 14 'fixes' solely for 'removed an obsolete introductory citation to a removed supporting manuscript'.
findings.why_relevant: The Oct versions are mathematically identical to the Sept/Oct-3 ones; any grading of the earlier text carries over unchanged. Also: the 'revised' companion editions the pointers now target contain no mathematical revisions either (checked for all five companions).

findings.item: Dv: In ExactBSD Oct-3, 01-introduction.tex:134 reads verbatim 'methods of \cite{B,C,Dv} provide the starting constructions.' The key Dv is NOT defined in references.tex of either the Oct-3 or the Oct-7 version (grep for \bibitem{Dv}: no hit), and no \bibitem{Dv} / @misc{Dv entry and no other \cite of Dv exists anywhere in the 749 preprint directories of the clone; so in the Oct-3 build it was a dangling key (would render as [?]). B = TwoPrimary and C = SelmerConverse (references.tex ll.~147-161), so 'Dv' was a further lettered companion in the same series. history.md states the Oct-7 fix 'removed an obsolete introductory citation to a removed supporting manuscript' -- i.e. Dv pointed to a supporting OAI manuscript that was removed from the collection BEFORE the public release (it is not one of the three Oct-7 withdrawals, which are the K3/Hodge papers: Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds (Sept-18), Algebraicity of Kuga-Satake Correspondences for K3 Surfaces (Oct-3), The rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces (Oct-4)). Its title and content are not recoverable from the clone. Dv is cited in no proof: its only occurrence is the intro sentence in 'Historical context and the integral problem'. The pdftotext extraction at scratchpad/openai_math_text/Exact-...txt l.186 is of the Oct-7 PDF ('methods of [24, 23]') and does not show the Oct-3 rendering.
findings.location: preprints/Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from-Low-Selmer-Corank-October-3-2026/build/sections/01-introduction.tex l.134; both versions' build/references.tex; history.md 'Fixes' bullet 5
findings.why_relevant: A removed (presumably defective or withdrawn pre-release) supporting manuscript once supplied 'starting constructions' for ExactBSD's finite-model/switching/theta methods. The Oct-7 text asserts B and C alone suffice; since the removed manuscript is unavailable, this assertion cannot be checked against what Dv contained. Not a proof-body dependence, so it does not by itself block use, but it is a provenance red flag for sections 3-8 of ExactBSD.

findings.item: WITHDRAWAL CROSS-CHECK: none of the six manuscripts (any version) is withdrawn; the only withdrawal-notice READMEs in the clone are the three K3/Hodge papers, and none of those is cited by any of the six (no OAI key in the six resolves outside the six). No dependence on a withdrawn manuscript. The only link to removed material is the dangling Dv key above.
findings.why_relevant: Clears the 'depends on withdrawn manuscript' kill condition for the chain; residual risk is the pre-release removal behind Dv.

findings.item: SEED HYPOTHESIS CHECK for the chain's theorems (all require full p^infty-Selmer corank s_q in {0,1} at SOME prime q; Pointwise2 and Goldfeld2 Thm 1.1 at q=2): seed E has rank 2, so s_q(E) >= 2 for every prime q (2, 3, 2243, 4547, 5843, all good ordinary and good supersingular primes) -- NO theorem in the six applies to E (K-RANK2). Twist E^{-7}: rank 0, L(E^{-7},1) != 0, Sha finite by Gross-Zagier-Kolyvagin, hence s_q(E^{-7}) = 0 for every q; so SelmerConverse/Goldfeld2 Thm 1.1 add nothing for E^{-7}, while TwoPrimary Thm 1.1 (v_2(#Sha(E^{-7})) = v_2(Q_{E^{-7}})) and ExactBSD Thm 1.1 eq (bsd-main) with r=0 (#Sha(E^{-7}/Q) = L(E^{-7},1)·#E^{-7}(Q)_tors^2 / (Omega·prod c_ell), total real period, both components) WOULD, if correct, determine #Sha(E^{-7}/Q) exactly -- serving only the lab's '#Sha(E^{-7})' sub-obligation, at grade IMPORTED_PREPRINT, and contingent on the whole chain Goldfeld2 -> SelmerConverse -> TwoPrimary -> ExactBSD plus Smith 2025 v1. Nothing in the six bears on FIN, ORDER9 or Q36 for E (rank 2; ExactBSD l.67: 'The low-Selmer-corank hypothesis is essential to the stated scope').
findings.why_relevant: Determines usability: zero direct applicability to E; one conditional, unrefereed route to #Sha(E^{-7}/Q), whose cost is verifying four AI manuscripts (no Lean) -- not a cost reduction of any existing lab computation.

findings.item: Downstream (reverse) citations, for completeness: SelmerConverse is imported by 'The p-adic section conjecture' (Sept-24 and Oct-6); Goldfeld2 and Pointwise2 are imported by 'Hilbert's tenth problem over the rational numbers' (Sept-24 and Oct-6). ExactBSD is cited by no other manuscript. Goldfeld2 (dated Sept 23) cites SelmerConverse and TwoPrimary (dated Sept 24) as 'subsequent companion' -- consistent with expository, not logical, dependence.
findings.why_relevant: Any defect in Goldfeld2 propagates to families 002, 004 (Hilbert 10 over Q) and 006, and SelmerConverse defects to the p-adic section conjecture; cosmetic for the seed audit.

notes: Scope: read-only audit of .tex/.bib/.md/.yaml in the untrusted openai/math clone (commit fd4aeeb); no code or build from it was run; diff -r and a scratchpad Python parser (python3 -I, scratchpad/scan/tools/oai_cites.py) were used only to read text. Machine edge list with every OAI cite location: scratchpad/scan/map/oai_cites_raw.json. Distinctions: (a) claimed-proved: Goldfeld2 Thm 1.1 (2-converse, 'main work of this paper'); SelmerConverse Thm 1.1 odd-p case; TwoPrimary Thm 1.1 (2-adic BSD in s_2<=1); ExactBSD Thm 1.1 odd-prime valuations; MeanRank Thm 1.2 tail estimate; Pointwise2 Thm 1.1. (b) literature imports named in the proofs: Smith arXiv:2503.17619v1 Thm 1.1 (Goldfeld2 Thm 1.2); Koymans-Smith arXiv:2606.31649v1 Thm 1.4 (MeanRank corollary; unverifiable offline); Dokchitser-Dokchitser 2010 Thm 1.4, BCDT 2001, Gross-Zagier 1986, Kolyvagin 1990, Kato 2004, Skinner-Urban 2014, Jetchev-Skinner-Wan 2017, Burungale-Flach 2024 (bibliographies). (c) OAI imports: as in the DAG. All grades: IMPORTED_PREPRINT (unrefereed, AI-generated, no Lean). Bottom line for the seed: no item in the six proves or cheapens FIN, ORDER9, Q36, Sha[p^infty]=0 at any named prime for E, lemma TH, or any existing lab computation; the sole conditional contribution is an exact #Sha(E^{-7}/Q) via ExactBSD+TwoPrimary for the rank-0 twist, which would require independently verifying the entire four-paper chain.
